name: Pelaliah
overview: Pelaliah was a male Levite known specifically as the son of Amzi, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:12. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation with Levi, a tribe set apart for priestly duties and service to God. Beyond this, Scripture provides limited additional information about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Pelaliah means 'YHWH intercedes in arbitration,' reflecting a divine involvement in justice or mediation. This proper name, found in Nehemiah 11:12, highlights a characteristic of God's active role in resolving disputes, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Pelaliah as the son of Amzi and infers Jeroham as his father, establishing a clear familial line within the Levite tribe. No further family relationships are documented beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Pelaliah's mention in Nehemiah 11:12 situates him within the post-exilic community of Levites who returned to Jerusalem, emphasizing the restoration of priestly families and their roles in worship and governance. His lineage underscores the faithfulness of God's covenant people in maintaining their sacred duties after exile. Though not prominent elsewhere, his presence in the biblical record affirms the continuity of God's ordained priestly line through Levi.
